title: Strada Launches Browser Automation: Agents Now Operate Web Portals and Systems That Don't Have APIs
summary: Strada agents can now log into carrier portals and legacy systems, complete back-office tasks on screen, and write back into the system of record.
body_markdown:
## How it works


Browser automation works like the rest of Strada. There is no code to write. You perform the task once, and the agent takes it from there.


We will follow one task the whole way through: updating the lienholder on a policy after a policyholder asks to change it. It is routine servicing work that normally means logging into a policy system by hand.


#### *Step 1: Record the task once*


Open a browser navigation node, start recording, and perform the task the way you always have. For the lienholder change, that means logging into the policy system, pulling up the policy, going to the lienholder section, and entering the new company. Strada captures each step as you go.


While you record, Strada's models work out the path through the system. From then on, the agent follows the same path every time, so its runs stay predictable. If the interface shifts in a small way, a button moves or a label is renamed, the agent adjusts and continues rather than breaking. It handles only minor changes on its own. Anything larger, and it stops and escalates instead of guessing its way through a screen it does not recognize.


#### *Step 2: Strada builds the workflow*


When you stop the recording, Strada turns the session into a workflow the agent can run. The path is fixed, but the data is not. In each case the agent pulls the values it needs from your systems, so a single recorded task can work through one policy after another, each with its own details.


#### *Step 3: Launch a run*


The agent then runs on its own. When a lienholder change comes in, it logs into the policy system, finds the policy, updates the lienholder, and saves the record, filling in that case's details as it goes. The task you recorded once runs as often as you need, with no one at the keyboard.


The agent checks the record before it acts, so it does not repeat a change that has already been made or move a setting the wrong way. Once it is finished, it reloads the screen and reads back the result rather than assuming the click landed. If what it finds does not match what it expected, the run stops.


#### *Step 4: Review every run*


Every run is recorded start to finish as video and saved to the run library. You can play back any run and see what the agent did: the screens it opened, the fields it touched, and the values it entered. A supervisor can spot-check a run the way they would review a new hire's work, and compliance has a record of what the agent did on each case.


Access is set up the way an insurer would want it. The agent logs in through a dedicated account you create, scoped to the permissions you grant, and you can revoke it at any time. Its credentials are injected at runtime and never reach the model, so there is nothing to leak. Strada keeps no separate copy of the data the agent handles. The only thing that persists is the session recording.
